Research findings and limitations

Scope and method: On 2026-10-30 all 550 STR files beneath ps3-eu-original:PS3_GAME/USRDIR were grouped by complete-file size and SHA-256. A bounded record walk decompressed sections and hashed exact 0x1607 payloads, retaining archive, section, decompressed record offset and embedded path. All 550 parsed without reported errors. Matching hashes indicate matching bytes, not interchangeable runtime resources. Counts are source occurrences, excluding converted outputs.

The 550 paths represent 439 distinct complete-file hashes. Six repeated groups contain 117 paths, accounting for 111 copies beyond one per group. Five groups are global localization containers repeated in 20 original USRDIR/<group>/text/ directories, each containing one LH2 record: 2919CD42.str (Spanish), 6255953C.str (Italian), 81DE1738.str (English), 95F47026.str (internal labels) and CD99D1BE.str (French). The sixth group contains 17 identical 2,048-byte STRs with zero sections, including USRDIR/colossaldonut/colossaldonut/zone08.str; their runtime purpose is unknown. The archive ledger lists every original path, size and hash.

The 25,988 asset records contain 15,357 distinct payloads; 3,117 groups recur, comprising 10,631 occurrences beyond one per hash. This includes records in identical archives. The 452 0x2207 bodies are excluded. Examples include assets/shared/bonebindings/player_default.bbn.PS3 (58 identical 1,304-byte occurrences), assets/shared/collision/npc_default.acs.PS3 (38 identical 884-byte occurrences) and global_cbgy.alb (11 identical 128-byte occurrences) across source archives. The payload ledger lists repeated hashes and all occurrences; paths are original metadata strings, including the build drive.

Among these records, 654 LH2 occurrences represent 346 distinct payloads; 529 ALB occurrences represent 519, and all 99 SMB occurrences differ by hash. The 77 .tox.PS3 occurrences represent 38 payloads; six 16-byte making-of timing resources in USRDIR/frontend/frontend.str share bytes despite different member names. Equal content alone does not prove a reference or shared runtime object.

A separate SHA-256 multiset comparison of all .LH2 files in each processed view found 654 files and 346 hashes in both Full and FullFlattened. Each view has exactly the same per-hash multiplicities as the 654 original STR LH2 records. This checks byte inventory, not a one-to-one path or archive mapping, and does not cover other formats or generated conversion files.

Repeated names can contain different data: case-insensitive embedded-path grouping within each archive finds eight groups, with 20 records beyond the first. All eight groups contain different payload hashes. For example, USRDIR/cheater/cheater/story_mode/story_mode_design.str has seven distinct StreamSetConfig records. Their section/offset coordinates and hashes are in the payload ledger. In the present Full output, the first and all six __str_duplicates__/sNNN_oXXXXXXXX/StreamSetConfig files were checked against their original payload hashes and match. The directory name denotes a repeated output path, not identical bytes. Other exports and historical extraction runs have not been exhaustively reconciled.

Exported-view example: USRDIR/loc/text/2919CD42.str has SHA-256 6ca6be194d34ab426ad85422ed381bdabf4f0dd2e5b4ef3a3dd5182787723949. Its member x:\build\PS3\pal_en\assets\localization\simpsons_global.es.LH2 has 150,468 bytes and SHA-256 c156f924f4a93f3f0d28456ab2f4500765fb219deecfc79f828dd5385444ff02. Both ps3-eu-extracted:L01_LandOfChocolate/text/2919CD42_str/build/PS3/pal_en/assets/localization/simpsons_global.es.LH2 and ps3-eu-flattened:L01_LandOfChocolate/text/2919cd42strAssetsLocalization/simpsons_global_bfc7c1.es.LH2 match that payload. This is one checked example, not a complete reconciliation of either output tree.

Extractor limitations: an older script could dump a section tail for an unnamed record, and rename-on-collision or rerunning into a populated directory can create extra outputs. The current BMS preserves record boundaries and gives repeated paths coordinate-qualified names; see the STR specification. This establishes real source copies and identifies possible artifact mechanisms; it does not establish that every unexplained export is an artifact or a game reference. Source data, extracted originals and generated conversions must be counted separately.
